instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups basmati rice in a strainer until the water runs clear. Put it in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to its lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop the onion and mince the garlic. Grate the ginger. That should be about 2 tbsp. Drain the chickpeas. Chop 1/4 cup cilantro.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet or wide pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika and salt. Stir for 1 minute, until the spices smell toasty.
Add the chickpeas, tomato puree and coconut milk. Stir, bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice with the cilantro on top.
method_notes: Live Eat Learn (4.72 from 74 ratings) is the quick one-pot version: onion, garlic and ginger, then garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric and smoked paprika, then chickpeas, tomato puree and coconut milk. The Wanderlust Kitchen (4.4 from 302) roasts cauliflower, purees half the sauce and adds a splash of vinegar, which makes it a 45 minute dish, so this version follows the lead. The lead suggests simmering uncovered to thicken, and says it freezes well in portions.
